reason: Python's commit hook stamps home_content_invalidated when transcript/user_corrections change; Go's stageHome writes only home_source_version and the control doc, so Home cannot tell content changed.

Python writes bounded, whitelisted recognition diagnostics on every persist; Go's finalizationFields writes none. Metadata is excluded from client JSON, so no privacy breach, but the diagnostic surface is lost for Go-owned rows.
Python stamps the recording speaker-scope index from speaker_id_scope on every write; Go writes no index, so recording rename cannot resolve scopes on a Go-owned row.
Python persists the resolved speaker model; Go writes no speaker_resolution, so a Go-owned row loses the resolved speaker labels.
Python writes sync_relevance (keep/review) with the relevance decision; Go's rules-only relevance never writes the field.
Python protects and writes user_corrections on every persist; Go's field map omits it, so user edits are dropped on a Go-owned row.
Companion flag for group 7; Go writes neither the corrections nor the compressed marker.
Python writes the row-local identity digest; Go writes none, so the identity-availability observation is missing for Go-owned rows.
Python always sets the compressed marker with the transcript; Go never writes it, so a reader cannot tell the stored shape from the flag.
Python maintains the 16-shard identity-availability counters; Go writes no shard document.
Python writes the effects transcript digest so a reprocess can prove the effects input; Go writes only its own go_finalization_notes_* keys.
Python writes an explicit discarded on every persist; Go writes it only when a discard patch exists, so the 13 rich cases carry no explicit false.
Python's notes dedupe reads notes_llm_input_hash; Go writes go_finalization_notes_input_hash instead, so alternating engines re-pay for notes.
Companion output hash for group 15; Go writes its own key, so Python's dedupe never sees a Go notes result.
Python writes the full relevance decision; Go writes one only when a serving/minimum patch supplies it, so the 13 rich cases have none.
Python records the summary stage in the pipeline ledger; Go's effects step writes no ledger row, so the stage history is missing.
Python runs the conv_discard model tier; Go's relevance is rules-only, so the paid discard call never happens on the Go side.
Python refreshes users/{uid}.ai_user_profile after processing; Go writes no profile refresh.
Python meters the conv_discard lane; Go never runs that lane, so no usage row.
Python meters the conv_structure lane; Go's usage rows omit it.
Python records the cost-exclusion reason when provider cost is missing; Go's usage metadata differs, so cost attribution is wrong.
Python counts missing-cost calls; Go's cost-status counts differ, so the cost ledger under-reports.

Plan-attributed conv_structure usage is missing on Go.
